correctness.rationale: A specified three-arrow injection decomposes into forced cycles and open directed paths. Deleting the former and contracting the latter removes exactly three units from the count of free units; completing the permutation gives total weight θ^κ θ^(overline{n−3}). To justify a finite all-n certificate, mark subsets of closed cycles and expand θ^κ in powers of θ−1. Each compatible fixed collection prescribes at most three sorted ranks and has a product of binomial counts with total degree at most three in u=i−1, v=n−i−2 (incompatible collections give zero). The degree bound holds for all nonnegative integer u,v including n=3. The binomial-product basis is triangular with diagonal ones on the ten nodes u+v≤3. Independently enumerating complete permutations by cycle count at these nodes and dividing each pattern weight polynomial by the rising factorial of length n−3 matched 60 rows, or 240 integer coefficients. Replay with node /workspace/review-checks/5-ewens-certificate.js. This is exact verification at degree-determining nodes, not numerical extrapolation. Subtracting consecutive rows gives the stated slopes; θ=1 gives each pattern weight C(n,3), hence probability 1/6.
residual_risks: No claim for nonconsecutive windows, longer patterns, or probability at θ=0. The check and proof do not establish originality.
